findings.message: Acceptance criterion 1 requires 'the specified Rework outcomes' for update, split, and escalate, but the ticket never defines them. The only text that would define them is `specs/rework.md`, which this same ticket creates, so the criterion defines itself. The plan-fixed properties of the stage are missing: Rework is an LLM stage (`rework` is already in `squatch/llm.py` LLM_SURFACES) that emits ONE composite rework-order artifact (updated ticket, split tickets, and/or an escalation element). The escalation element is consumed by the ladder's journal-derived rung and is never written into ticket frontmatter. The consumed handoff carries `approval_invalidated=True`, which forces re-review. Split children record a supersedes link to the stem they replace. Without these, a known-deep implementation can pass with any outcome shape.
findings.paved_road: Restate criterion 1 as separate checkable assertions in `tests/test_rework.py`. (a) `specs/rework.md` lints through `squatch.specs.load_spec` as surface `rework` with a single composite rework-order `emits` type. (b) Under the fake LLM, an update order yields an updated ticket for the handoff stem. (c) A split order yields child tickets, each with a supersedes link to the parent stem. (d) An escalate order yields an escalation element with ticket frontmatter left unchanged. (e) Every consumed `UnresolvedConflictHandoff` keeps its approval invalidated, so the resulting work is re-reviewed. Keep the rest of the fence, Context, and scope-out exactly as authored.
